reason: The answer to “Has the company implemented multi-factor authentication systems?”—“MFA implemented only on some systems”—is broadly consistent with, but less specific than, the dossier: MFA is active for ordinary operations-system accounts, VPN, email and the jump host, while it is absent from the legacy RDP maintenance account and two active cloud-console administrative accounts (AR-04, AR-07). Aurora Grid has assessed authentication methods using all three factors required by PR.AA-03_P1—account privileges, system criticality and permitted operations—and concluded that every account on both relevant systems requires MFA (AR-01, AR-07). This aligns with the guidance that authentication strength should reflect asset classification (V5-ENISA-0050-01). However, the identified privileged and remote-access accounts remain active without the MFA required by that assessment, without documented derogations; the legacy RDP path also lacks connection-origin restrictions (AR-04, AR-07). Thus, the required risk assessment exists and risk-commensurate authentication is implemented for part of the applicable scope, but concrete gaps prevent full satisfaction of PR.AA-03_P1 (AR-04, AR-07).
